title: Preflight: inference shift notes — Zara Malik
body:
Morning preflight notes (shift 06:30-14:30)

Context:
- Night shift saw a transient p99 spike on hosted-api (region us-west-2) between 02:10-02:35. Rough pattern: large requests (seq_len ~1200) + heavy new user traffic.
- Symptoms: increased tail latency, a handful of rejection 429s from batcher, and two infra autoscale events that didn’t fully clear the queue.

Quick checks to run (order):
1) ingest last hour of metrics: `curl -s ${REDWOOD_METRICS}/query?query=p99_latency` -> focus on model=redwood-7b-int8 and redwood-13b-q4
2) check prefix-cache hit rate: grafana -> "Prefix cache: hit rate by model" (time window 02:00-03:00)
3) review batcher logs for partition evictions: `kubectl logs -l app=batcher -n serving --since=3h | rg "evict|drop|429"`
4) check KV cache eviction metric: `kv_cache/evictions_total` and correlate with `active_sessions`

Immediate observations:
- Preliminary: KV cache eviction spikes line up with drop in prefix-cache-hit-rate. Eviction reason: memory pressure on nodes hosting model redwood-13b-q4 on instance-gpu-2.
- Batcher emitted backpressure -> 429s. The backpressure threshold (config: max_queue_ms=75) appears too aggressive for long-sequence requests.
- One suspect: recent PR that tuned LRU window (PR #4982) may be too eager for large sessions. Opening ticket to double-check assumptions.

Repro steps to validate locally:
- Use replay harness: `tools/replay --trace traces/long_seq_user_20260311.json --model redwood-13b-q4 --simulate-latency`
- Run analyzer to watch kv-cache behavior: `python infra/kv_tools/observe.py --trace-id 20260311-long1`

Immediate action items (today):
- [ ] Raise kv cache threshold for redwood-13b-q4 from 60% -> 70% (temporary) and observe 2-hour window (Ishaan)
- [ ] Temporarily increase batcher max_queue_ms to 150 for critical pool (Mina)
- [ ] Add more verbose logging around eviction reason (kernel vs oom vs manual) in batcher (me) -> small PR to repo (target: PR to master by EOD)
- [ ] Create an incident note in RT-2434 (me) summarizing findings + mitigation steps

Follow-ups (not urgent):
- Add a metric: `prefix_cache/object_size_distribution` to detect large prefixes causing evictions
- Hypothesis: quantized int4 path increases working set for KV cache due to denser keys — run microbench to measure kv-cache memory per token for q4 vs int8
- Postmortem draft if spike repeats for next 48h

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Could try soft eviction tiers: prefer evicting sessions with zero-recent-access rather than largest-first; combination of LRU + size weighted.
- Consider burst queue that bypasses backpressure for authenticated enterprise customers (route to dedicated pool) — product question (talk to PM later)
- Coffee

Scratch commands (save these):
- `kubectl get pods -n serving -l model=redwood-13b-q4 -o wide`
- `curl -s ${REDWOOD_METRICS}/api/v1/query_range?query=kv_cache_evictions_total&start=2026-03-12T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-13T08:00:00Z`

Open TODO log (quick):
- PR: add eviction-reason label to metric (me) -> branch: metric/evict-label
- Ticket: follow-up microbench q4 vs int8 (Ishaan) -> RT-2460
- Doc: add runbook section for long-seq incidents (me + Mina) -> draft in confluence

End-of-shift handoff (notes for night):
- If p99 remains > target, roll back the LRU window change (revert PR #4982) and revert batcher queue to old thresholds.
- Contact SRE if node memory pressure persists after threshold changes: slack @sre-oncall.

Random brain dump (put here so I don’t lose it):
- There was a weird trace where kv lookup latency jumped but CPU was low — maybe NUMA or memcpy cost on kernel path when sequence > 1024. Add sampling profiler for sequences > 1024.

Timestamped quick logs: 
- 2026-03-12 07:15 - pulled logs; saw 37 eviction events in 20m window
- 2026-03-12 07:42 - increased batcher queue (test) -> immediate reduction in 429s but slight p95 increase
summary: Shift preflight + triage notes focused on KV cache evictions, batcher backpressure, temporary mitigations, and followups. Actionables assigned to Ishaan, Mina, and Zara.
